pull_request.title: fix(shell): treat PowerShell directive paths literally
pull_request.body:
When the PowerShell temporary directory contains wildcard characters such as `temp[1]`, `wt switch` can finish without changing the parent shell's directory. The directive file is written, but the wrapper treats its path as a wildcard during lookup and cleanup, leaving the file behind.

Use `-LiteralPath` for all four directive-file operations. Add a regression that checks both the directory change and removal of the temporary file, and refresh the generated PowerShell snapshot.

Validation: all 4 PowerShell integration tests pass with all features enabled, including the new regression. The shell-generation snapshot test, pre-commit checks (including clippy), doctests and rustdoc also pass. The original template reproduced the failure on Windows PowerShell 5; the corrected template switches directories and leaves no directive file on both Windows PowerShell 5 and PowerShell 7.6.9.

The full `hook pre-merge --yes` gate did not pass on this Windows host: 4,693 passed, 74 failed, 40 skipped. Failures include configuration/statusline snapshots, switch tests and the performance helper CLI; those failures and snapshots are outside this change and were not accepted or modified.
